## Gaussian

```{r}
set.seed(246)

library(dlnm)
library(splines)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Dimensoes e blocos
# -------------------------------------------------------------

n_epi <- 520L
n_days <- 86L
n_blocks <- 20L

if (n_epi %% n_blocks != 0L) {
  stop("`n_epi` deve ser divisivel por `n_blocks`.")
}

block <- factor(rep(
  paste0("B", sprintf("%02d", seq_len(n_blocks))),
  each = n_epi / n_blocks
))

time_values <- 0:(n_days - 1L)
lag_for_time <- (n_days - 1L) - time_values

# time 85 -> lag 0; time 0 -> lag 85

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Matrizes cronologicas de exposicao
# -------------------------------------------------------------

tmean_time <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_epi, ncol = n_days)
wetness_time <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_epi, ncol = n_days)
rain_time <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_epi, ncol = n_days)

colnames(tmean_time) <- paste0("time_", time_values)
colnames(wetness_time) <- paste0("time_", time_values)
colnames(rain_time) <- paste0("time_", time_values)

# =============================================================
# 1. SIMULAR HISTORICOS CLIMATICOS CRONOLOGICOS
# =============================================================

for (i in seq_len(n_epi)) {
  temp_shift <- rnorm(1L, 0, 2.0)
  wetness_shift <- rnorm(1L, 0, 2.8)
  rain_shift <- rnorm(1L, 0, 0.40)
  
  ar_temp <- as.numeric(arima.sim(
    model = list(ar = 0.72), n = n_days, sd = 1.0
  ))
  ar_wetness <- as.numeric(arima.sim(
    model = list(ar = 0.78), n = n_days, sd = 1.5
  ))
  ar_rain <- as.numeric(arima.sim(
    model = list(ar = 0.58), n = n_days, sd = 0.50
  ))
  
  tmean <- 25.5 + temp_shift +
    3.3 * sin(2 * pi * time_values / 85 + runif(1L, -0.35, 0.35)) +
    ar_temp
  tmean <- pmin(pmax(tmean, 15), 36)
  
  wetness <- 10.5 + wetness_shift +
    2.4 * sin(2 * pi * time_values / 46 + runif(1L, -0.50, 0.50)) +
    ar_wetness
  wetness <- pmin(pmax(wetness, 0), 24)
  
  rain_probability <- plogis(
    -0.80 + rain_shift +
      0.50 * sin(2 * pi * time_values / 35 + runif(1L, -0.50, 0.50)) +
      ar_rain
  )
  rainy_day <- rbinom(n_days, size = 1L, prob = rain_probability)
  rain_amount <- rgamma(n_days, shape = 1.7, scale = 5.2)
  rain <- pmin(rainy_day * rain_amount, 40)
  
  tmean_time[i, ] <- tmean
  wetness_time[i, ] <- wetness
  rain_time[i, ] <- rain
}

# =============================================================
# 2. RELACOES EXPOSICAO-RESPOSTA VERDADEIRAS
# =============================================================

# Temperatura: resposta unimodal, otimo proximo de 26 C
temp_response <- exp(-0.5 * ((tmean_time - 26) / 3.2)^2)

# Molhamento: resposta sigmoide acima de aproximadamente 11 h
wetness_response <- plogis((wetness_time - 11) / 1.8)

# Chuva: resposta crescente com saturacao
rain_response <- plogis((sqrt(rain_time) - 2.1) / 0.80)

# =============================================================
# 3. FUNCOES VERDADEIRAS DE LAG
# =============================================================

# Pesos avaliados em lag_for_time preservam a ordem cronologica.
temp_lag_weights_time <- dnorm(lag_for_time, mean = 20, sd = 9)
temp_lag_weights_time <- temp_lag_weights_time / sum(temp_lag_weights_time)

wetness_lag_weights_time <- dnorm(lag_for_time, mean = 14, sd = 8)
wetness_lag_weights_time <- wetness_lag_weights_time /
  sum(wetness_lag_weights_time)

rain_lag_weights_time <- dnorm(lag_for_time, mean = 8, sd = 6)
rain_lag_weights_time <- rain_lag_weights_time / sum(rain_lag_weights_time)

# =============================================================
# 4. EFEITOS CUMULATIVOS VERDADEIROS
# =============================================================

true_temp_effect <- as.numeric(temp_response %*% temp_lag_weights_time)
true_wetness_effect <- as.numeric(
  wetness_response %*% wetness_lag_weights_time
)
true_rain_effect <- as.numeric(rain_response %*% rain_lag_weights_time)

standardize_effect <- function(x) {
  out <- as.numeric(scale(x))
  if (any(!is.finite(out))) {
    stop("Nao foi possivel padronizar um efeito cumulativo verdadeiro.")
  }
  out
}

temp_effect_z <- standardize_effect(true_temp_effect)
wetness_effect_z <- standardize_effect(true_wetness_effect)
rain_effect_z <- standardize_effect(true_rain_effect)

# =============================================================
# 5. EFEITO ALEATORIO VERDADEIRO DE BLOCO
# =============================================================

block_sd <- 0.80
block_effect <- rnorm(n_blocks, mean = 0, sd = block_sd)
names(block_effect) <- levels(block)
block_re <- block_effect[as.character(block)]

# =============================================================
# 6. GERAR A MEDIA GAUSSIANA NA ESCALA IDENTIDADE
# =============================================================
#
# O desfecho representa intensidade ou taxa continua de estruturas
# do patogeno. A media basal e mantida suficientemente acima de zero.
# =============================================================

eta_true <- 12 +
  1.25 * temp_effect_z +
  1.70 * wetness_effect_z +
  1.10 * rain_effect_z +
  block_re

mu_epi <- eta_true

# =============================================================
# 7. GERAR O DESFECHO GAUSSIANO
# =============================================================
#
# Y_i | X_i, block_i ~ Normal(mu_i, gaussian_sigma^2)
# A semente e os parametros foram escolhidos para produzir y > 0.
# Como a Gaussiana possui suporte real, a positividade e conferida
# explicitamente e nenhum valor e truncado ou corrigido.
# =============================================================

gaussian_sigma <- 1.50

y_epi <- rnorm(n_epi, mean = mu_epi, sd = gaussian_sigma)
y_epi <- as.numeric(y_epi)

if (any(y_epi <= 0)) {
  stop(
    "A realizacao Gaussiana produziu y <= 0. Aumente a media basal ou reduza `gaussian_sigma`."
  )
}

# =============================================================
# 8. CRIAR O CONJUNTO LONG EM ORDEM CRONOLOGICA
# =============================================================

sim_data_gaussian <- data.frame(
  epi_id = rep(seq_len(n_epi), each = n_days),
  block = rep(block, each = n_days),
  time = rep(time_values, times = n_epi),
  tmean = as.vector(t(tmean_time)),
  wetness = as.vector(t(wetness_time)),
  rain = as.vector(t(rain_time)),
  y = rep(y_epi, each = n_days)
)

sim_data_gaussian <- sim_data_gaussian[
  order(sim_data_gaussian$epi_id, sim_data_gaussian$time),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
rownames(sim_data_gaussian) <- NULL

# =============================================================
# 9. CHECAGENS DA SIMULACAO
# =============================================================

if (!all(table(sim_data_gaussian$epi_id) == n_days)) {
  stop("Cada epidemia deve possuir exatamente 86 observacoes temporais.")
}

if (length(unique(sim_data_gaussian$epi_id)) != n_epi) {
  stop("O numero de epidemias simuladas esta incorreto.")
}

blocks_per_epidemic <- tapply(
  sim_data_gaussian$block,
  sim_data_gaussian$epi_id,
  function(x) length(unique(x))
)
if (!all(blocks_per_epidemic == 1L)) {
  stop("Pelo menos uma epidemia foi associada a mais de um bloco.")
}

block_epidemic_table <- table(
  unique(sim_data_gaussian[c("epi_id", "block")])$block
)
if (!all(block_epidemic_table == n_epi / n_blocks)) {
  stop("O numero de epidemias por bloco esta incorreto.")
}

time_validation <- tapply(
  sim_data_gaussian$time,
  sim_data_gaussian$epi_id,
  function(x) {
    !anyDuplicated(x) &&
      !is.unsorted(x, strictly = TRUE) &&
      identical(as.integer(x), time_values)
  }
)
if (!all(time_validation)) {
  stop("A estrutura temporal nao esta cronologica ou contem duplicatas.")
}

outcomes_per_epidemic <- tapply(
  sim_data_gaussian$y,
  sim_data_gaussian$epi_id,
  function(x) length(unique(x))
)
if (!all(outcomes_per_epidemic == 1L)) {
  stop("Pelo menos uma epidemia possui mais de um valor de y.")
}

if (anyNA(sim_data_gaussian)) {
  stop("A simulacao produziu valores ausentes.")
}

if (any(!is.finite(sim_data_gaussian$tmean)) ||
    any(!is.finite(sim_data_gaussian$wetness)) ||
    any(!is.finite(sim_data_gaussian$rain)) ||
    any(!is.finite(sim_data_gaussian$y))) {
  stop("A simulacao produziu valores nao finitos.")
}

if (!is.numeric(sim_data_gaussian$y) || any(sim_data_gaussian$y <= 0)) {
  stop("Neste exemplo Gaussiano, y deve ser continuo e estritamente positivo.")
}

# =============================================================
# 10. RESUMOS DIAGNOSTICOS
# =============================================================

cat("Numero de epidemias:", n_epi, "\n")
cat("Observacoes por epidemia:", n_days, "\n")
cat("Numero de blocos:", n_blocks, "\n")
cat("Epidemias por bloco:", n_epi / n_blocks, "\n")
cat("Media de y:", round(mean(y_epi), 3), "\n")
cat("Desvio-padrao de y:", round(sd(y_epi), 3), "\n")
cat("Minimo de y:", round(min(y_epi), 3), "\n")
cat("Maximo de y:", round(max(y_epi), 3), "\n")
cat("Media de mu:", round(mean(mu_epi), 3), "\n")
cat("Desvio-padrao residual verdadeiro:", gaussian_sigma, "\n")
cat("Desvio-padrao verdadeiro do bloco:", block_sd, "\n")

head(sim_data_gaussian)
tail(sim_data_gaussian)
summary(sim_data_gaussian$tmean)
summary(sim_data_gaussian$wetness)
summary(sim_data_gaussian$rain)
summary(y_epi)
print(block_epidemic_table)

true_effect_correlation <- cor(cbind(
  temperature = temp_effect_z,
  wetness = wetness_effect_z,
  rain = rain_effect_z
))
print(round(true_effect_correlation, 3))

hist(
  y_epi,
  breaks = 30,
  main = "Intensidade de estruturas do patogeno, Gaussiana",
  xlab = "Intensidade ou taxa continua (> 0)",
  col = "gray80",
  border = "white"
)

plot(
  mu_epi,
  y_epi,
  pch = 16,
  col = grDevices::adjustcolor("steelblue", alpha.f = 0.45),
  xlab = "Media verdadeira esperada, mu",
  ylab = "Intensidade observada, y",
  main = "Resposta Gaussiana simulada"
)
abline(a = 0, b = 1, lty = 2, col = "gray40")

# =============================================================
# 11. OBJETO AUXILIAR COM A VERDADE DA SIMULACAO
# =============================================================

simulation_truth_gaussian <- data.frame(
  epi_id = seq_len(n_epi),
  block = block,
  block_effect = as.numeric(block_re),
  true_temp_effect = true_temp_effect,
  true_wetness_effect = true_wetness_effect,
  true_rain_effect = true_rain_effect,
  temp_effect_z = temp_effect_z,
  wetness_effect_z = wetness_effect_z,
  rain_effect_z = rain_effect_z,
  eta_true = eta_true,
  mu = mu_epi,
  gaussian_sigma = gaussian_sigma,
  y = y_epi
)

writexl::write_xlsx(sim_data_gaussian,"gaussian_data.xlsx")
```

## spaMM dataset

### Ano dependente

```{r}
set.seed(20260918)

library(dlnm)
library(splines)

n_epi <- 520L
n_days <- 86L
n_blocks <- 20L

time_values <- 0:(n_days - 1L)
lag_for_time <- (n_days - 1L) - time_values

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. COORDENADAS ESPACIAIS
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Grade 26 x 20, com pequena irregularidade nas coordenadas.
# As unidades sao arbitrarias e representam distancia Euclidiana.

spatial_grid <- expand.grid(
  x_coord = seq(0, 100, length.out = 26L),
  y_coord = seq(0, 76, length.out = 20L)
)

spatial_grid$x_coord <- spatial_grid$x_coord + runif(n_epi, -0.8, 0.8)
spatial_grid$y_coord <- spatial_grid$y_coord + runif(n_epi, -0.8, 0.8)
spatial_grid$epi_id <- seq_len(n_epi)
spatial_grid$block <- factor(
  paste0("B", sprintf("%02d", rep(seq_len(n_blocks), each = 26L)))
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. PROCESSO ESPACIAL MATERN VERDADEIRO
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# Correlacao Matérn exponencial, equivalente a nu = 0.5.
# cor(d) = exp(-d / spatial_range)

coord_matrix <- as.matrix(spatial_grid[c("x_coord", "y_coord")])
distance_matrix <- as.matrix(stats::dist(coord_matrix))

spatial_range <- 18
spatial_sd <- 0.35
spatial_nugget <- 1e-8

spatial_correlation <- exp(-distance_matrix / spatial_range)
diag(spatial_correlation) <- diag(spatial_correlation) + spatial_nugget

spatial_root <- chol(spatial_correlation)
spatial_effect <- as.numeric(
  t(spatial_root) %*% rnorm(n_epi, mean = 0, sd = spatial_sd)
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. MATRIZES CRONOLOGICAS DE EXPOSICAO
# -------------------------------------------------------------

tmean_time <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_epi, ncol = n_days)
wetness_time <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_epi, ncol = n_days)
rain_time <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = n_epi, ncol = n_days)

# Tendencias espaciais climaticas suaves, diferentes do campo residual.
temp_spatial_trend <- scale(
  0.60 * spatial_grid$x_coord - 0.35 * spatial_grid$y_coord
)[, 1]

wetness_spatial_trend <- scale(
  -0.25 * spatial_grid$x_coord + 0.70 * spatial_grid$y_coord
)[, 1]

rain_spatial_trend <- scale(
  0.35 * spatial_grid$x_coord + 0.45 * spatial_grid$y_coord
)[, 1]

for (i in seq_len(n_epi)) {
  temp_shift <- 1.25 * temp_spatial_trend[i] + rnorm(1L, 0, 1.2)
  wetness_shift <- 1.80 * wetness_spatial_trend[i] + rnorm(1L, 0, 1.7)
  rain_shift <- 0.25 * rain_spatial_trend[i] + rnorm(1L, 0, 0.25)
  
  ar_temp <- as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = 0.72), n_days, sd = 1.0))
  ar_wetness <- as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = 0.78), n_days, sd = 1.5))
  ar_rain <- as.numeric(arima.sim(list(ar = 0.58), n_days, sd = 0.50))
  
  tmean <- 25.5 + temp_shift +
    3.3 * sin(2 * pi * time_values / 85 + runif(1L, -0.35, 0.35)) +
    ar_temp
  tmean <- pmin(pmax(tmean, 15), 36)
  
  wetness <- 10.5 + wetness_shift +
    2.4 * sin(2 * pi * time_values / 46 + runif(1L, -0.50, 0.50)) +
    ar_wetness
  wetness <- pmin(pmax(wetness, 0), 24)
  
  rain_probability <- plogis(
    -0.80 + rain_shift +
      0.50 * sin(2 * pi * time_values / 35 + runif(1L, -0.50, 0.50)) +
      ar_rain
  )
  rainy_day <- rbinom(n_days, 1L, rain_probability)
  rain <- rainy_day * rgamma(n_days, shape = 1.7, scale = 5.2)
  rain <- pmin(rain, 40)
  
  tmean_time[i, ] <- tmean
  wetness_time[i, ] <- wetness
  rain_time[i, ] <- rain
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. RELACOES EXPOSICAO-RESPOSTA E LAG VERDADEIRAS
# -------------------------------------------------------------

temp_response <- exp(-0.5 * ((tmean_time - 26) / 3.2)^2)
wetness_response <- plogis((wetness_time - 11) / 1.8)
rain_response <- plogis((sqrt(rain_time) - 2.1) / 0.80)

temp_lag_weights <- dnorm(lag_for_time, mean = 20, sd = 9)
temp_lag_weights <- temp_lag_weights / sum(temp_lag_weights)

wetness_lag_weights <- dnorm(lag_for_time, mean = 14, sd = 8)
wetness_lag_weights <- wetness_lag_weights / sum(wetness_lag_weights)

rain_lag_weights <- dnorm(lag_for_time, mean = 8, sd = 6)
rain_lag_weights <- rain_lag_weights / sum(rain_lag_weights)

true_temp_effect <- as.numeric(temp_response %*% temp_lag_weights)
true_wetness_effect <- as.numeric(wetness_response %*% wetness_lag_weights)
true_rain_effect <- as.numeric(rain_response %*% rain_lag_weights)

standardize_effect <- function(x) {
  out <- as.numeric(scale(x))
  if (any(!is.finite(out))) stop("Falha ao padronizar efeito verdadeiro.")
  out
}

temp_effect_z <- standardize_effect(true_temp_effect)
wetness_effect_z <- standardize_effect(true_wetness_effect)
rain_effect_z <- standardize_effect(true_rain_effect)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. DESFECHO POISSON COM EFEITO ESPACIAL
# -------------------------------------------------------------
# O efeito espacial entra como componente latente residual.

eta_true <- log(10) +
  0.38 * temp_effect_z +
  0.52 * wetness_effect_z +
  0.34 * rain_effect_z +
  spatial_effect

mu_epi <- exp(eta_true)
y_epi <- as.integer(rpois(n_epi, lambda = mu_epi))

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. DADOS LONG PARA O EPIEXPOSURE
# -------------------------------------------------------------

sim_data_spatial <- data.frame(
  epi_id = rep(seq_len(n_epi), each = n_days),
  block = rep(spatial_grid$block, each = n_days),
  time = rep(time_values, times = n_epi),
  x_coord = rep(spatial_grid$x_coord, each = n_days),
  y_coord = rep(spatial_grid$y_coord, each = n_days),
  tmean = as.vector(t(tmean_time)),
  wetness = as.vector(t(wetness_time)),
  rain = as.vector(t(rain_time)),
  y = rep(y_epi, each = n_days)
)

sim_data_spatial <- sim_data_spatial[
  order(sim_data_spatial$epi_id, sim_data_spatial$time),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]
rownames(sim_data_spatial) <- NULL

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. VERDADE DA SIMULACAO, UMA LINHA POR EPIDEMIA
# -------------------------------------------------------------

simulation_truth_spatial <- data.frame(
  epi_id = seq_len(n_epi),
  block = spatial_grid$block,
  x_coord = spatial_grid$x_coord,
  y_coord = spatial_grid$y_coord,
  spatial_effect = spatial_effect,
  true_temp_effect = true_temp_effect,
  true_wetness_effect = true_wetness_effect,
  true_rain_effect = true_rain_effect,
  temp_effect_z = temp_effect_z,
  wetness_effect_z = wetness_effect_z,
  rain_effect_z = rain_effect_z,
  eta_true = eta_true,
  mu = mu_epi,
  y = y_epi
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. CHECAGENS
# -------------------------------------------------------------

stopifnot(
  nrow(sim_data_spatial) == n_epi * n_days,
  all(table(sim_data_spatial$epi_id) == n_days),
  all(sim_data_spatial$y >= 0L),
  !anyNA(sim_data_spatial),
  all(is.finite(sim_data_spatial$x_coord)),
  all(is.finite(sim_data_spatial$y_coord))
)

space_per_epidemic <- tapply(
  seq_len(nrow(sim_data_spatial)),
  sim_data_spatial$epi_id,
  function(ii) {
    length(unique(sim_data_spatial$x_coord[ii])) == 1L &&
      length(unique(sim_data_spatial$y_coord[ii])) == 1L
  }
)
stopifnot(all(space_per_epidemic))

cat("Epidemias/localidades:", n_epi, "\n")
cat("Dias por epidemia:", n_days, "\n")
cat("Media de y:", round(mean(y_epi), 3), "\n")
cat("Variancia marginal de y:", round(var(y_epi), 3), "\n")
cat("SD espacial verdadeiro:", spatial_sd, "\n")
cat("Alcance usado na simulacao:", spatial_range, "\n")

# Visualizacao do campo espacial verdadeiro
plot(
  spatial_grid$x_coord,
  spatial_grid$y_coord,
  pch = 21,
  bg = hcl.colors(30, "Blue-Red 3")[
    cut(spatial_effect, breaks = 30, include.lowest = TRUE)
  ],
  asp = 1,
  xlab = "x_coord",
  ylab = "y_coord",
  main = "Efeito espacial Matérn verdadeiro"
)

writexl::write_xlsx(sim_data_spatial,"spamm_st_poisson.xlsx")
```

### Ano independente
```{r}
# =============================================================
# SIMULACAO DLNM ESPACIAL COM CAMPOS MATERN INDEPENDENTES POR ANO
#
# 130 localidades x 4 anos = 520 epidemias
# 86 dias por epidemia
# Uma contagem Poisson final por combinacao localidade-ano
#
# Modelo espacial pretendido:
#
# Matern(1 | x_coord + y_coord %in% year)
#
# Cada ano possui uma realizacao espacial independente, mas todos
# os anos compartilham os mesmos parametros de correlacao espacial.
#
# Neste mecanismo gerador, `year` nao possui efeito fixo diretamente
# sobre a resposta. Sua funcao e identificar campos espaciais
# independentes e permitir condicoes climaticas distintas entre anos.
# =============================================================

set.seed(20260919)

library(dlnm)
library(splines)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. DIMENSOES
# -------------------------------------------------------------

n_locations <- 130L
years <- 2022:2025
n_years <- length(years)

n_epi <- n_locations * n_years
n_days <- 86L

time_values <- 0:(n_days - 1L)

# Para a avaliacao final em time = 85:
# time 85 corresponde ao lag 0
# time 0 corresponde ao lag 85
lag_for_time <- (n_days - 1L) - time_values

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. LOCALIDADES E COORDENADAS FIXAS
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# A grade possui 13 x 10 = 130 localidades.
#
# As mesmas localidades sao observadas nos quatro anos.
# Portanto, cada location_id conserva suas coordenadas ao longo
# dos anos, mas cada combinacao localidade-ano recebe um epi_id
# diferente.
# -------------------------------------------------------------

location_grid <- expand.grid(
  x_coord = seq(
    from = 0,
    to = 96,
    length.out = 13L
  ),
  y_coord = seq(
    from = 0,
    to = 72,
    length.out = 10L
  )
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(location_grid) == n_locations
)

location_grid$x_coord <- (
  location_grid$x_coord +
    runif(
      n_locations,
      min = -0.8,
      max = 0.8
    )
)

location_grid$y_coord <- (
  location_grid$y_coord +
    runif(
      n_locations,
      min = -0.8,
      max = 0.8
    )
)

location_grid$location_id <- paste0(
  "L",
  sprintf(
    "%03d",
    seq_len(n_locations)
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. TABELA COM UMA LINHA POR EPIDEMIA
# -------------------------------------------------------------

epidemic_table <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(
    years,
    function(current_year) {
      data.frame(
        location_id = location_grid$location_id,
        year = current_year,
        x_coord = location_grid$x_coord,
        y_coord = location_grid$y_coord,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }
  )
)

rownames(epidemic_table) <- NULL

epidemic_table$epi_id <- paste(
  epidemic_table$location_id,
  epidemic_table$year,
  sep = "_"
)

epidemic_table$year <- factor(
  epidemic_table$year,
  levels = years
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. BLOCOS EXPERIMENTAIS ESPECIFICOS POR ANO
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Existem 10 blocos por ano, com 13 localidades em cada bloco.
#
# A numeracao dos blocos seria repetida em cada ano. Por isso,
# block_id combina ano e bloco, impedindo que B01 de 2022 seja
# tratado como o mesmo nivel de B01 de 2023.
# -------------------------------------------------------------

blocks_per_year <- 10L
locations_per_block <- n_locations / blocks_per_year

stopifnot(
  locations_per_block == as.integer(
    locations_per_block
  )
)

block_within_year <- rep(
  paste0(
    "B",
    sprintf(
      "%02d",
      seq_len(blocks_per_year)
    )
  ),
  each = locations_per_block
)

epidemic_table$block <- rep(
  block_within_year,
  times = n_years
)

epidemic_table$block_id <- factor(
  paste(
    epidemic_table$year,
    epidemic_table$block,
    sep = "_"
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. MATRIZ DE DISTANCIAS ENTRE LOCALIDADES
# -------------------------------------------------------------

coordinate_matrix <- as.matrix(
  location_grid[
    c(
      "x_coord",
      "y_coord"
    )
  ]
)

distance_matrix <- as.matrix(
  stats::dist(
    coordinate_matrix
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. PARAMETROS DO PROCESSO ESPACIAL VERDADEIRO
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Utilizamos uma correlacao exponencial:
#
# cor(d) = exp(-d / spatial_range)
#
# Essa correlacao corresponde ao caso Matérn com nu = 0.5.
#
# Cada ano possui uma realizacao independente do campo espacial.
# Entretanto, spatial_range e spatial_sd sao iguais para todos
# os anos, de acordo com a interpretacao de:
#
# Matern(1 | x_coord + y_coord %in% year)
# -------------------------------------------------------------

spatial_range <- 18
spatial_sd <- 0.35
spatial_nugget <- 1e-8

spatial_correlation <- exp(
  -distance_matrix / spatial_range
)

diag(spatial_correlation) <- (
  diag(spatial_correlation) +
    spatial_nugget
)

spatial_root <- chol(
  spatial_correlation
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. SIMULAR UM CAMPO ESPACIAL INDEPENDENTE PARA CADA ANO
# -------------------------------------------------------------

spatial_effect_by_year <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = n_locations,
  ncol = n_years,
  dimnames = list(
    location_grid$location_id,
    as.character(years)
  )
)

for (j in seq_along(years)) {
  spatial_effect_by_year[, j] <- as.numeric(
    t(spatial_root) %*%
      rnorm(
        n = n_locations,
        mean = 0,
        sd = spatial_sd
      )
  )
}

epidemic_table$spatial_effect <- NA_real_

for (j in seq_along(years)) {
  current_year <- as.character(
    years[j]
  )

  current_rows <- (
    as.character(
      epidemic_table$year
    ) == current_year
  )

  location_match <- match(
    epidemic_table$location_id[current_rows],
    rownames(
      spatial_effect_by_year
    )
  )

  epidemic_table$spatial_effect[current_rows] <- (
    spatial_effect_by_year[
      location_match,
      current_year
    ]
  )
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. EFEITO ALEATORIO CONVENCIONAL DE BLOCO
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Este componente e distinto do efeito espacial.
#
# block_id representa agrupamento experimental discreto.
# spatial_effect representa autocorrelacao espacial continua.
# -------------------------------------------------------------

block_sd <- 0.18

block_levels <- levels(
  epidemic_table$block_id
)

block_effect_values <- rnorm(
  n = length(block_levels),
  mean = 0,
  sd = block_sd
)

names(block_effect_values) <- block_levels

epidemic_table$block_effect <- block_effect_values[
  as.character(
    epidemic_table$block_id
  )
]

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. TENDENCIAS CLIMATICAS ESPACIAIS DAS LOCALIDADES
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# As exposicoes possuem tendencias espaciais suaves.
#
# Essas tendencias representam variacao geografica observada nas
# condicoes climaticas e sao distintas do campo espacial residual.
# -------------------------------------------------------------

temp_location_trend <- as.numeric(
  scale(
    0.60 * location_grid$x_coord -
      0.35 * location_grid$y_coord
  )
)

wetness_location_trend <- as.numeric(
  scale(
    -0.25 * location_grid$x_coord +
      0.70 * location_grid$y_coord
  )
)

rain_location_trend <- as.numeric(
  scale(
    0.35 * location_grid$x_coord +
      0.45 * location_grid$y_coord
  )
)

names(temp_location_trend) <- (
  location_grid$location_id
)

names(wetness_location_trend) <- (
  location_grid$location_id
)

names(rain_location_trend) <- (
  location_grid$location_id
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. DESLOCAMENTOS CLIMATICOS ENTRE ANOS
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Esses valores produzem safras com condicoes climaticas medias
# ligeiramente diferentes.
#
# Eles nao representam um efeito fixo direto de year sobre y.
# Os anos influenciam a resposta somente por meio dos historicos
# climaticos simulados e dos campos espaciais independentes.
# -------------------------------------------------------------

temperature_year_shift <- c(
  "2022" = -0.8,
  "2023" = 0.4,
  "2024" = 1.0,
  "2025" = -0.2
)

wetness_year_shift <- c(
  "2022" = 0.7,
  "2023" = -0.4,
  "2024" = 0.9,
  "2025" = -0.2
)

rain_year_shift <- c(
  "2022" = 0.15,
  "2023" = -0.12,
  "2024" = 0.28,
  "2025" = -0.05
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. MATRIZES CRONOLOGICAS DE EXPOSICAO
# -------------------------------------------------------------

tmean_time <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = n_epi,
  ncol = n_days
)

wetness_time <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = n_epi,
  ncol = n_days
)

rain_time <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = n_epi,
  ncol = n_days
)

colnames(tmean_time) <- paste0(
  "time_",
  time_values
)

colnames(wetness_time) <- paste0(
  "time_",
  time_values
)

colnames(rain_time) <- paste0(
  "time_",
  time_values
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 12. SIMULAR HISTORICOS CLIMATICOS
# -------------------------------------------------------------

for (i in seq_len(n_epi)) {
  current_location <- epidemic_table$location_id[i]

  current_year <- as.character(
    epidemic_table$year[i]
  )

  temp_shift <- (
    1.25 * temp_location_trend[current_location] +
      temperature_year_shift[current_year] +
      rnorm(
        1L,
        mean = 0,
        sd = 1.1
      )
  )

  wetness_shift <- (
    1.80 * wetness_location_trend[current_location] +
      wetness_year_shift[current_year] +
      rnorm(
        1L,
        mean = 0,
        sd = 1.5
      )
  )

  rain_shift <- (
    0.25 * rain_location_trend[current_location] +
      rain_year_shift[current_year] +
      rnorm(
        1L,
        mean = 0,
        sd = 0.22
      )
  )

  ar_temp <- as.numeric(
    arima.sim(
      model = list(
        ar = 0.72
      ),
      n = n_days,
      sd = 1.0
    )
  )

  ar_wetness <- as.numeric(
    arima.sim(
      model = list(
        ar = 0.78
      ),
      n = n_days,
      sd = 1.5
    )
  )

  ar_rain <- as.numeric(
    arima.sim(
      model = list(
        ar = 0.58
      ),
      n = n_days,
      sd = 0.50
    )
  )

  tmean <- (
    25.5 +
      temp_shift +
      3.3 * sin(
        2 * pi * time_values / 85 +
          runif(
            1L,
            min = -0.35,
            max = 0.35
          )
      ) +
      ar_temp
  )

  tmean <- pmin(
    pmax(
      tmean,
      15
    ),
    36
  )

  wetness <- (
    10.5 +
      wetness_shift +
      2.4 * sin(
        2 * pi * time_values / 46 +
          runif(
            1L,
            min = -0.50,
            max = 0.50
          )
      ) +
      ar_wetness
  )

  wetness <- pmin(
    pmax(
      wetness,
      0
    ),
    24
  )

  rain_probability <- plogis(
    -0.80 +
      rain_shift +
      0.50 * sin(
        2 * pi * time_values / 35 +
          runif(
            1L,
            min = -0.50,
            max = 0.50
          )
      ) +
      ar_rain
  )

  rainy_day <- rbinom(
    n = n_days,
    size = 1L,
    prob = rain_probability
  )

  rain_amount <- rgamma(
    n = n_days,
    shape = 1.7,
    scale = 5.2
  )

  rain <- rainy_day * rain_amount

  rain <- pmin(
    rain,
    40
  )

  tmean_time[i, ] <- tmean
  wetness_time[i, ] <- wetness
  rain_time[i, ] <- rain
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 13. RELACOES EXPOSICAO-RESPOSTA VERDADEIRAS
# -------------------------------------------------------------

# Temperatura:
# relacao unimodal com maior favorabilidade proxima de 26 graus.
temp_response <- exp(
  -0.5 *
    (
      (tmean_time - 26) / 3.2
    )^2
)

# Molhamento foliar:
# resposta sigmoide com aumento acima de aproximadamente 11 horas.
wetness_response <- plogis(
  (wetness_time - 11) / 1.8
)

# Chuva:
# resposta crescente com saturacao.
rain_response <- plogis(
  (
    sqrt(rain_time) - 2.1
  ) / 0.80
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 14. FUNCOES VERDADEIRAS DE LAG
# -------------------------------------------------------------

temp_lag_weights <- dnorm(
  lag_for_time,
  mean = 20,
  sd = 9
)

temp_lag_weights <- (
  temp_lag_weights /
    sum(temp_lag_weights)
)

wetness_lag_weights <- dnorm(
  lag_for_time,
  mean = 14,
  sd = 8
)

wetness_lag_weights <- (
  wetness_lag_weights /
    sum(wetness_lag_weights)
)

rain_lag_weights <- dnorm(
  lag_for_time,
  mean = 8,
  sd = 6
)

rain_lag_weights <- (
  rain_lag_weights /
    sum(rain_lag_weights)
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 15. EFEITOS CLIMATICOS CUMULATIVOS VERDADEIROS
# -------------------------------------------------------------

true_temp_effect <- as.numeric(
  temp_response %*%
    temp_lag_weights
)

true_wetness_effect <- as.numeric(
  wetness_response %*%
    wetness_lag_weights
)

true_rain_effect <- as.numeric(
  rain_response %*%
    rain_lag_weights
)

standardize_effect <- function(x) {
  out <- as.numeric(
    scale(x)
  )

  if (any(!is.finite(out))) {
    stop(
      "Falha ao padronizar efeito verdadeiro."
    )
  }

  out
}

temp_effect_z <- standardize_effect(
  true_temp_effect
)

wetness_effect_z <- standardize_effect(
  true_wetness_effect
)

rain_effect_z <- standardize_effect(
  true_rain_effect
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 16. PREDITOR LINEAR VERDADEIRO
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Cada epidemia recebe:
#
# 1. efeitos climaticos distribuidos no tempo;
# 2. efeito espacial especifico do ano;
# 3. efeito aleatorio convencional de bloco.
#
# Nao existe um efeito fixo direto de year no preditor linear.
# A variavel year define somente:
#
# 1. os campos espaciais independentes;
# 2. os deslocamentos dos historicos climaticos simulados.
#
# Portanto, o mecanismo gerador fica alinhado ao modelo:
#
# y_model ~
#   1 +
#   cb_* +
#   (1 | block_id) +
#   Matern(1 | x_coord + y_coord %in% year)
# -------------------------------------------------------------

eta_true <- (
  log(10) +
    0.38 * temp_effect_z +
    0.52 * wetness_effect_z +
    0.34 * rain_effect_z +
    epidemic_table$spatial_effect +
    epidemic_table$block_effect
)

mu_epi <- exp(
  eta_true
)

y_epi <- as.integer(
  rpois(
    n = n_epi,
    lambda = mu_epi
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 17. DADOS LONGOS PARA O EPIEXPOSURE
# -------------------------------------------------------------

sim_data_spatial_year <- data.frame(
  epi_id = rep(
    epidemic_table$epi_id,
    each = n_days
  ),
  location_id = rep(
    epidemic_table$location_id,
    each = n_days
  ),
  year = rep(
    epidemic_table$year,
    each = n_days
  ),
  block = rep(
    epidemic_table$block,
    each = n_days
  ),
  block_id = rep(
    epidemic_table$block_id,
    each = n_days
  ),
  time = rep(
    time_values,
    times = n_epi
  ),
  x_coord = rep(
    epidemic_table$x_coord,
    each = n_days
  ),
  y_coord = rep(
    epidemic_table$y_coord,
    each = n_days
  ),
  tmean = as.vector(
    t(tmean_time)
  ),
  wetness = as.vector(
    t(wetness_time)
  ),
  rain = as.vector(
    t(rain_time)
  ),
  y = rep(
    y_epi,
    each = n_days
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

sim_data_spatial_year <- sim_data_spatial_year[
  order(
    sim_data_spatial_year$epi_id,
    sim_data_spatial_year$time
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

rownames(
  sim_data_spatial_year
) <- NULL

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 18. OBJETO COM A VERDADE DA SIMULACAO
# -------------------------------------------------------------

simulation_truth_spatial_year <- data.frame(
  epi_id = epidemic_table$epi_id,
  location_id = epidemic_table$location_id,
  year = epidemic_table$year,
  block = epidemic_table$block,
  block_id = epidemic_table$block_id,
  x_coord = epidemic_table$x_coord,
  y_coord = epidemic_table$y_coord,
  spatial_effect = epidemic_table$spatial_effect,
  block_effect = epidemic_table$block_effect,
  true_temp_effect = true_temp_effect,
  true_wetness_effect = true_wetness_effect,
  true_rain_effect = true_rain_effect,
  temp_effect_z = temp_effect_z,
  wetness_effect_z = wetness_effect_z,
  rain_effect_z = rain_effect_z,
  eta_true = eta_true,
  mu = mu_epi,
  y = y_epi,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 19. CHECAGENS
# -------------------------------------------------------------

stopifnot(
  nrow(epidemic_table) == n_epi,
  nrow(sim_data_spatial_year) == n_epi * n_days,
  length(unique(sim_data_spatial_year$epi_id)) == n_epi,
  length(unique(sim_data_spatial_year$location_id)) == n_locations,
  length(unique(sim_data_spatial_year$year)) == n_years,
  all(table(sim_data_spatial_year$epi_id) == n_days),
  all(sim_data_spatial_year$y >= 0L),
  !anyNA(sim_data_spatial_year),
  all(is.finite(sim_data_spatial_year$x_coord)),
  all(is.finite(sim_data_spatial_year$y_coord))
)

# Cada epi_id deve possuir exatamente:
# uma localidade, um ano, um bloco e um par de coordenadas.
constant_within_epidemic <- tapply(
  seq_len(
    nrow(sim_data_spatial_year)
  ),
  sim_data_spatial_year$epi_id,
  function(ii) {
    length(
      unique(
        sim_data_spatial_year$location_id[ii]
      )
    ) == 1L &&
      length(
        unique(
          sim_data_spatial_year$year[ii]
        )
      ) == 1L &&
      length(
        unique(
          sim_data_spatial_year$block_id[ii]
        )
      ) == 1L &&
      length(
        unique(
          sim_data_spatial_year$x_coord[ii]
        )
      ) == 1L &&
      length(
        unique(
          sim_data_spatial_year$y_coord[ii]
        )
      ) == 1L
  }
)

stopifnot(
  all(
    constant_within_epidemic
  )
)

# Cada localidade deve aparecer exatamente uma vez em cada ano.
location_year_table <- table(
  epidemic_table$location_id,
  epidemic_table$year
)

stopifnot(
  all(
    location_year_table == 1L
  )
)

# As coordenadas devem ser constantes para uma localidade ao longo
# dos anos.
coordinate_consistency <- tapply(
  seq_len(
    nrow(epidemic_table)
  ),
  epidemic_table$location_id,
  function(ii) {
    length(
      unique(
        epidemic_table$x_coord[ii]
      )
    ) == 1L &&
      length(
        unique(
          epidemic_table$y_coord[ii]
        )
      ) == 1L
  }
)

stopifnot(
  all(
    coordinate_consistency
  )
)

# Cada block_id deve pertencer a apenas um ano.


writexl::write_xlsx(sim_data_spatial_year,"sim_data_spatial_year.xlsx")
```

### Epidemic replicate independente

```{r}
# =============================================================
# SIMULACAO DLNM ESPACIAL COM CAMPOS MATERN INDEPENDENTES
# ENTRE REPETICOES EPIDEMIOLOGICAS
#
# 130 localidades x 4 repeticoes = 520 epidemias
# 86 dias por epidemia
# Uma contagem Poisson final por combinacao:
#
# location_id x epidemic_replicate
#
# Modelo espacial pretendido:
#
# Matern(
#   1 | x_coord + y_coord %in% epidemic_replicate
# )
#
# Cada repeticao representa uma nova realizacao completa e
# independente do mesmo processo epidemiologico.
#
# Cada repeticao possui:
#
# 1. novos historicos climaticos;
# 2. um novo campo espacial residual;
# 3. uma nova resposta final da doenca.
#
# As repeticoes compartilham:
#
# 1. as mesmas localidades;
# 2. a mesma escala temporal de 86 dias;
# 3. as mesmas relacoes exposicao-resposta;
# 4. as mesmas funcoes de lag;
# 5. os mesmos parametros do processo espacial.
#
# epidemic_replicate nao possui efeito fixo direto sobre y.
# Sua funcao no modelo e identificar campos espaciais
# independentes.
# =============================================================

set.seed(20260920)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. DIMENSOES
# -------------------------------------------------------------

n_locations <- 130L

epidemic_replicates <- paste0(
  "Replicate_",
  seq_len(4L)
)

n_replicates <- length(
  epidemic_replicates
)

n_epi <- n_locations * n_replicates
n_days <- 86L

time_values <- 0:(n_days - 1L)

# Para a avaliacao final em time = 85:
#
# time 85 corresponde ao lag 0
# time 84 corresponde ao lag 1
# ...
# time 0 corresponde ao lag 85

lag_for_time <- (
  n_days - 1L
) - time_values

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. LOCALIDADES E COORDENADAS FIXAS
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# A grade possui 13 x 10 = 130 localidades.
#
# As mesmas localidades sao utilizadas nas quatro repeticoes.
# Portanto, cada location_id conserva suas coordenadas.
#
# Cada combinacao localidade-repeticao recebe um epi_id diferente.
# -------------------------------------------------------------

location_grid <- expand.grid(
  x_coord = seq(
    from = 0,
    to = 96,
    length.out = 13L
  ),
  y_coord = seq(
    from = 0,
    to = 72,
    length.out = 10L
  )
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(location_grid) == n_locations
)

location_grid$x_coord <- (
  location_grid$x_coord +
    runif(
      n = n_locations,
      min = -0.8,
      max = 0.8
    )
)

location_grid$y_coord <- (
  location_grid$y_coord +
    runif(
      n = n_locations,
      min = -0.8,
      max = 0.8
    )
)

location_grid$location_id <- paste0(
  "L",
  sprintf(
    "%03d",
    seq_len(n_locations)
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. TABELA COM UMA LINHA POR EPIDEMIA
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Cada epidemia corresponde a uma combinacao unica:
#
# location_id x epidemic_replicate
# -------------------------------------------------------------

epidemic_table <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(
    epidemic_replicates,
    function(current_replicate) {
      data.frame(
        location_id = location_grid$location_id,
        epidemic_replicate = current_replicate,
        x_coord = location_grid$x_coord,
        y_coord = location_grid$y_coord,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }
  )
)

rownames(
  epidemic_table
) <- NULL

epidemic_table$epi_id <- paste(
  epidemic_table$location_id,
  epidemic_table$epidemic_replicate,
  sep = "_"
)

epidemic_table$epidemic_replicate <- factor(
  epidemic_table$epidemic_replicate,
  levels = epidemic_replicates
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. BLOCOS ESPECIFICOS DE CADA REPETICAO
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Existem 10 blocos em cada repeticao, com 13 localidades por
# bloco.
#
# block_id combina a repeticao e o bloco. Assim, B01 da primeira
# repeticao nao e tratado como o mesmo nivel de B01 da segunda
# repeticao.
#
# block_id representa um intercepto aleatorio convencional.
# Esse componente e distinto do campo espacial Matérn.
# -------------------------------------------------------------

blocks_per_replicate <- 10L

locations_per_block <- (
  n_locations /
    blocks_per_replicate
)

stopifnot(
  locations_per_block ==
    as.integer(
      locations_per_block
    )
)

block_within_replicate <- rep(
  paste0(
    "B",
    sprintf(
      "%02d",
      seq_len(
        blocks_per_replicate
      )
    )
  ),
  each = locations_per_block
)

epidemic_table$block <- rep(
  block_within_replicate,
  times = n_replicates
)

epidemic_table$block_id <- factor(
  paste(
    epidemic_table$epidemic_replicate,
    epidemic_table$block,
    sep = "_"
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. MATRIZ DE DISTANCIAS ENTRE LOCALIDADES
# -------------------------------------------------------------

coordinate_matrix <- as.matrix(
  location_grid[
    c(
      "x_coord",
      "y_coord"
    )
  ]
)

distance_matrix <- as.matrix(
  stats::dist(
    coordinate_matrix
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. PARAMETROS DO PROCESSO ESPACIAL VERDADEIRO
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Utilizamos uma correlacao exponencial:
#
# cor(d) = exp(-d / spatial_range)
#
# Essa correlacao corresponde ao caso Matérn com nu = 0.5.
#
# Cada repeticao recebe uma realizacao espacial independente.
#
# Entretanto, todas compartilham spatial_range e spatial_sd,
# conforme a interpretacao de:
#
# Matern(
#   1 | x_coord + y_coord %in% epidemic_replicate
# )
# -------------------------------------------------------------

spatial_range <- 18
spatial_sd <- 0.35
spatial_nugget <- 1e-8

spatial_correlation <- exp(
  -distance_matrix /
    spatial_range
)

diag(
  spatial_correlation
) <- (
  diag(
    spatial_correlation
  ) +
    spatial_nugget
)

spatial_root <- chol(
  spatial_correlation
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. CAMPOS ESPACIAIS INDEPENDENTES ENTRE REPETICOES
# -------------------------------------------------------------

spatial_effect_by_replicate <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = n_locations,
  ncol = n_replicates,
  dimnames = list(
    location_grid$location_id,
    epidemic_replicates
  )
)

for (j in seq_along(epidemic_replicates)) {
  spatial_effect_by_replicate[, j] <- as.numeric(
    t(spatial_root) %*%
      rnorm(
        n = n_locations,
        mean = 0,
        sd = spatial_sd
      )
  )
}

epidemic_table$spatial_effect <- NA_real_

for (j in seq_along(epidemic_replicates)) {
  current_replicate <- epidemic_replicates[j]

  current_rows <- (
    as.character(
      epidemic_table$epidemic_replicate
    ) == current_replicate
  )

  location_match <- match(
    epidemic_table$location_id[current_rows],
    rownames(
      spatial_effect_by_replicate
    )
  )

  epidemic_table$spatial_effect[current_rows] <- (
    spatial_effect_by_replicate[
      location_match,
      current_replicate
    ]
  )
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. EFEITO ALEATORIO CONVENCIONAL DE BLOCO
# -------------------------------------------------------------

block_sd <- 0.18

block_levels <- levels(
  epidemic_table$block_id
)

block_effect_values <- rnorm(
  n = length(
    block_levels
  ),
  mean = 0,
  sd = block_sd
)

names(
  block_effect_values
) <- block_levels

epidemic_table$block_effect <- block_effect_values[
  as.character(
    epidemic_table$block_id
  )
]

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. TENDENCIAS CLIMATICAS ESPACIAIS
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# As exposicoes possuem tendencias espaciais suaves que permanecem
# comparaveis entre as repeticoes.
#
# Cada repeticao ainda recebe novas series temporais e novas
# realizacoes dos componentes estocasticos das exposicoes.
# -------------------------------------------------------------

temp_location_trend <- as.numeric(
  scale(
    0.60 * location_grid$x_coord -
      0.35 * location_grid$y_coord
  )
)

wetness_location_trend <- as.numeric(
  scale(
    -0.25 * location_grid$x_coord +
      0.70 * location_grid$y_coord
  )
)

rain_location_trend <- as.numeric(
  scale(
    0.35 * location_grid$x_coord +
      0.45 * location_grid$y_coord
  )
)

names(
  temp_location_trend
) <- location_grid$location_id

names(
  wetness_location_trend
) <- location_grid$location_id

names(
  rain_location_trend
) <- location_grid$location_id

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. MATRIZES CRONOLOGICAS DE EXPOSICAO
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Ao contrario do exemplo anterior com cultivares, as repeticoes
# independentes nao recebem historicos climaticos identicos.
#
# Cada combinacao localidade-repeticao possui seu proprio historico
# de 86 dias.
# -------------------------------------------------------------

tmean_time <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = n_epi,
  ncol = n_days
)

wetness_time <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = n_epi,
  ncol = n_days
)

rain_time <- matrix(
  NA_real_,
  nrow = n_epi,
  ncol = n_days
)

colnames(tmean_time) <- paste0(
  "time_",
  time_values
)

colnames(wetness_time) <- paste0(
  "time_",
  time_values
)

colnames(rain_time) <- paste0(
  "time_",
  time_values
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. SIMULAR HISTORICOS CLIMATICOS DE CADA REPETICAO
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Os deslocamentos abaixo criam variabilidade estocastica entre as
# repeticoes, sem adicionar um efeito fixo direto de repeticao em y.
#
# Eventuais diferencas na resposta causadas por esses deslocamentos
# sao explicadas pelas proprias exposicoes e suas funcoes de lag.
# -------------------------------------------------------------

for (i in seq_len(n_epi)) {
  current_location <- epidemic_table$location_id[i]

  temp_shift <- (
    1.25 * temp_location_trend[current_location] +
      rnorm(
        n = 1L,
        mean = 0,
        sd = 1.1
      )
  )

  wetness_shift <- (
    1.80 * wetness_location_trend[current_location] +
      rnorm(
        n = 1L,
        mean = 0,
        sd = 1.5
      )
  )

  rain_shift <- (
    0.25 * rain_location_trend[current_location] +
      rnorm(
        n = 1L,
        mean = 0,
        sd = 0.22
      )
  )

  ar_temp <- as.numeric(
    arima.sim(
      model = list(
        ar = 0.72
      ),
      n = n_days,
      sd = 1.0
    )
  )

  ar_wetness <- as.numeric(
    arima.sim(
      model = list(
        ar = 0.78
      ),
      n = n_days,
      sd = 1.5
    )
  )

  ar_rain <- as.numeric(
    arima.sim(
      model = list(
        ar = 0.58
      ),
      n = n_days,
      sd = 0.50
    )
  )

  tmean <- (
    25.5 +
      temp_shift +
      3.3 * sin(
        2 * pi * time_values / 85 +
          runif(
            n = 1L,
            min = -0.35,
            max = 0.35
          )
      ) +
      ar_temp
  )

  tmean <- pmin(
    pmax(
      tmean,
      15
    ),
    36
  )

  wetness <- (
    10.5 +
      wetness_shift +
      2.4 * sin(
        2 * pi * time_values / 46 +
          runif(
            n = 1L,
            min = -0.50,
            max = 0.50
          )
      ) +
      ar_wetness
  )

  wetness <- pmin(
    pmax(
      wetness,
      0
    ),
    24
  )

  rain_probability <- plogis(
    -0.80 +
      rain_shift +
      0.50 * sin(
        2 * pi * time_values / 35 +
          runif(
            n = 1L,
            min = -0.50,
            max = 0.50
          )
      ) +
      ar_rain
  )

  rainy_day <- rbinom(
    n = n_days,
    size = 1L,
    prob = rain_probability
  )

  rain_amount <- rgamma(
    n = n_days,
    shape = 1.7,
    scale = 5.2
  )

  rain <- rainy_day *
    rain_amount

  rain <- pmin(
    rain,
    40
  )

  tmean_time[i, ] <- tmean
  wetness_time[i, ] <- wetness
  rain_time[i, ] <- rain
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 12. RELACOES EXPOSICAO-RESPOSTA VERDADEIRAS
# -------------------------------------------------------------

# Temperatura:
# relacao unimodal com maior favorabilidade proxima de 26 graus.

temp_response <- exp(
  -0.5 *
    (
      (tmean_time - 26) /
        3.2
    )^2
)

# Molhamento foliar:
# resposta sigmoide com aumento acima de aproximadamente 11 horas.

wetness_response <- plogis(
  (
    wetness_time - 11
  ) / 1.8
)

# Chuva:
# resposta crescente com saturacao.

rain_response <- plogis(
  (
    sqrt(
      rain_time
    ) - 2.1
  ) / 0.80
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 13. FUNCOES VERDADEIRAS DE LAG
# -------------------------------------------------------------

temp_lag_weights <- dnorm(
  lag_for_time,
  mean = 20,
  sd = 9
)

temp_lag_weights <- (
  temp_lag_weights /
    sum(
      temp_lag_weights
    )
)

wetness_lag_weights <- dnorm(
  lag_for_time,
  mean = 14,
  sd = 8
)

wetness_lag_weights <- (
  wetness_lag_weights /
    sum(
      wetness_lag_weights
    )
)

rain_lag_weights <- dnorm(
  lag_for_time,
  mean = 8,
  sd = 6
)

rain_lag_weights <- (
  rain_lag_weights /
    sum(
      rain_lag_weights
    )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 14. EFEITOS CLIMATICOS CUMULATIVOS VERDADEIROS
# -------------------------------------------------------------

true_temp_effect <- as.numeric(
  temp_response %*%
    temp_lag_weights
)

true_wetness_effect <- as.numeric(
  wetness_response %*%
    wetness_lag_weights
)

true_rain_effect <- as.numeric(
  rain_response %*%
    rain_lag_weights
)

standardize_effect <- function(x) {
  out <- as.numeric(
    scale(x)
  )

  if (any(!is.finite(out))) {
    stop(
      "Falha ao padronizar efeito verdadeiro."
    )
  }

  out
}

temp_effect_z <- standardize_effect(
  true_temp_effect
)

wetness_effect_z <- standardize_effect(
  true_wetness_effect
)

rain_effect_z <- standardize_effect(
  true_rain_effect
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 15. PREDITOR LINEAR VERDADEIRO
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Cada epidemia recebe:
#
# 1. efeitos climaticos distribuidos no tempo;
# 2. efeito espacial especifico da repeticao;
# 3. efeito aleatorio convencional de bloco.
#
# Nao existe efeito fixo direto de epidemic_replicate.
#
# epidemic_replicate identifica somente as realizacoes
# independentes do campo espacial.
#
# O mecanismo gerador corresponde conceitualmente a:
#
# y_model ~
#   1 +
#   cb_* +
#   (1 | block_id) +
#   Matern(
#     1 | x_coord + y_coord %in% epidemic_replicate
#   )
# -------------------------------------------------------------

eta_true <- (
  log(10) +
    0.38 * temp_effect_z +
    0.52 * wetness_effect_z +
    0.34 * rain_effect_z +
    epidemic_table$spatial_effect +
    epidemic_table$block_effect
)

mu_epi <- exp(
  eta_true
)

y_epi <- as.integer(
  rpois(
    n = n_epi,
    lambda = mu_epi
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 16. DADOS LONGOS PARA O EPIEXPOSURE
# -------------------------------------------------------------

sim_data_spatial_replicate <- data.frame(
  epi_id = rep(
    epidemic_table$epi_id,
    each = n_days
  ),
  location_id = rep(
    epidemic_table$location_id,
    each = n_days
  ),
  epidemic_replicate = rep(
    epidemic_table$epidemic_replicate,
    each = n_days
  ),
  block = rep(
    epidemic_table$block,
    each = n_days
  ),
  block_id = rep(
    epidemic_table$block_id,
    each = n_days
  ),
  time = rep(
    time_values,
    times = n_epi
  ),
  x_coord = rep(
    epidemic_table$x_coord,
    each = n_days
  ),
  y_coord = rep(
    epidemic_table$y_coord,
    each = n_days
  ),
  tmean = as.vector(
    t(
      tmean_time
    )
  ),
  wetness = as.vector(
    t(
      wetness_time
    )
  ),
  rain = as.vector(
    t(
      rain_time
    )
  ),
  y = rep(
    y_epi,
    each = n_days
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

sim_data_spatial_replicate <- sim_data_spatial_replicate[
  order(
    sim_data_spatial_replicate$epi_id,
    sim_data_spatial_replicate$time
  ),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

rownames(
  sim_data_spatial_replicate
) <- NULL

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 17. VERDADE DA SIMULACAO
# -------------------------------------------------------------

simulation_truth_spatial_replicate <- data.frame(
  epi_id = epidemic_table$epi_id,
  location_id = epidemic_table$location_id,
  epidemic_replicate = epidemic_table$epidemic_replicate,
  block = epidemic_table$block,
  block_id = epidemic_table$block_id,
  x_coord = epidemic_table$x_coord,
  y_coord = epidemic_table$y_coord,
  spatial_effect = epidemic_table$spatial_effect,
  block_effect = epidemic_table$block_effect,
  true_temp_effect = true_temp_effect,
  true_wetness_effect = true_wetness_effect,
  true_rain_effect = true_rain_effect,
  temp_effect_z = temp_effect_z,
  wetness_effect_z = wetness_effect_z,
  rain_effect_z = rain_effect_z,
  eta_true = eta_true,
  mu = mu_epi,
  y = y_epi,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 18. CHECAGENS GERAIS
# -------------------------------------------------------------

stopifnot(
  nrow(epidemic_table) == n_epi,
  nrow(sim_data_spatial_replicate) == n_epi * n_days,
  length(
    unique(
      sim_data_spatial_replicate$epi_id
    )
  ) == n_epi,
  length(
    unique(
      sim_data_spatial_replicate$location_id
    )
  ) == n_locations,
  length(
    unique(
      sim_data_spatial_replicate$epidemic_replicate
    )
  ) == n_replicates,
  all(
    table(
      sim_data_spatial_replicate$epi_id
    ) == n_days
  ),
  all(
    sim_data_spatial_replicate$y >= 0L
  ),
  !anyNA(
    sim_data_spatial_replicate
  ),
  all(
    is.finite(
      sim_data_spatial_replicate$x_coord
    )
  ),
  all(
    is.finite(
      sim_data_spatial_replicate$y_coord
    )
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 19. CONSTANCIA DENTRO DE CADA EPIDEMIA
# -------------------------------------------------------------

constant_within_epidemic <- tapply(
  seq_len(
    nrow(
      sim_data_spatial_replicate
    )
  ),
  sim_data_spatial_replicate$epi_id,
  function(ii) {
    length(
      unique(
        sim_data_spatial_replicate$location_id[ii]
      )
    ) == 1L &&
      length(
        unique(
          sim_data_spatial_replicate$epidemic_replicate[ii]
        )
      ) == 1L &&
      length(
        unique(
          sim_data_spatial_replicate$block_id[ii]
        )
      ) == 1L &&
      length(
        unique(
          sim_data_spatial_replicate$x_coord[ii]
        )
      ) == 1L &&
      length(
        unique(
          sim_data_spatial_replicate$y_coord[ii]
        )
      ) == 1L
  }
)

stopifnot(
  all(
    constant_within_epidemic
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 20. DESENHO LOCALIDADE X REPETICAO
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Cada localidade deve aparecer exatamente uma vez em cada
# repeticao epidemiologica.
# -------------------------------------------------------------

location_replicate_table <- table(
  epidemic_table$location_id,
  epidemic_table$epidemic_replicate
)

stopifnot(
  all(
    location_replicate_table == 1L
  )
)

# As coordenadas devem permanecer constantes para uma localidade
# em todas as repeticoes.

coordinate_consistency <- tapply(
  seq_len(
    nrow(
      epidemic_table
    )
  ),
  epidemic_table$location_id,
  function(ii) {
    length(
      unique(
        epidemic_table$x_coord[ii]
      )
    ) == 1L &&
      length(
        unique(
          epidemic_table$y_coord[ii]
        )
      ) == 1L
  }
)

stopifnot(
  all(
    coordinate_consistency
  )
)

# Cada block_id deve pertencer a apenas uma repeticao.

block_replicate_consistency <- tapply(
  seq_len(
    nrow(
      epidemic_table
    )
  ),
  epidemic_table$block_id,
  function(ii) {
    length(
      unique(
        epidemic_table$epidemic_replicate[ii]
      )
    ) == 1L
  }
)

stopifnot(
  all(
    block_replicate_consistency
  )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 21. CHECAR QUE OS HISTORICOS VARIAM ENTRE REPETICOES
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Como as repeticoes sao independentes, uma mesma localidade nao
# deve receber automaticamente o mesmo historico climatico nas
# quatro repeticoes.
# -------------------------------------------------------------

climate_means_by_replicate <- aggregate(
  cbind(
    tmean,
    wetness,
    rain
  ) ~ epidemic_replicate,
  data = sim_data_spatial_replicate,
  FUN = mean
)

print(
  climate_means_by_replicate
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 22. INDEPENDENCIA DOS CAMPOS ESPACIAIS
# -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Os campos espaciais foram gerados de forma independente.
#
# As correlacoes amostrais nao precisam ser exatamente zero, mas
# nenhuma correlacao entre as realizacoes foi imposta.
# -------------------------------------------------------------

spatial_field_correlations <- cor(
  spatial_effect_by_replicate
)

print(
  round(
    spatial_field_correlations,
    3
  )
)

cat(
  "Localidades:",
  n_locations,
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Repeticoes epidemiologicas:",
  n_replicates,
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Epidemias:",
  n_epi,
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Dias por epidemia:",
  n_days,
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Media de y:",
  round(
    mean(
      y_epi
    ),
    3
  ),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Variancia marginal de y:",
  round(
    var(
      y_epi
    ),
    3
  ),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "SD espacial verdadeiro:",
  spatial_sd,
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Variancia espacial verdadeira:",
  spatial_sd^2,
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Alcance espacial usado:",
  spatial_range,
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Nu Matérn equivalente:",
  0.5,
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "SD verdadeiro de bloco:",
  block_sd,
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "Variancia verdadeira de bloco:",
  block_sd^2,
  "\n"
)

print(
  table(
    epidemic_table$epidemic_replicate
  )
)

response_summary_by_replicate <- aggregate(
  cbind(
    y,
    mu
  ) ~ epidemic_replicate,
  data = simulation_truth_spatial_replicate,
  FUN = mean
)

print(
  response_summary_by_replicate
)

# Confirmar que nao existe efeito fixo artificial de repeticao.

stopifnot(
  !"replicate_effect" %in%
    names(
      epidemic_table
    ),
  !"replicate_effect" %in%
    names(
      simulation_truth_spatial_replicate
    )
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 23. VISUALIZAR OS CAMPOS ESPACIAIS
# -------------------------------------------------------------

old_par <- par(
  mfrow = c(
    2,
    2
  ),
  mar = c(
    4,
    4,
    3,
    1
  )
)

spatial_breaks <- seq(
  min(
    spatial_effect_by_replicate
  ),
  max(
    spatial_effect_by_replicate
  ),
  length.out = 31L
)

spatial_colors <- hcl.colors(
  n = 30L,
  palette = "Blue-Red 3"
)

for (j in seq_along(epidemic_replicates)) {
  color_index <- cut(
    spatial_effect_by_replicate[, j],
    breaks = spatial_breaks,
    include.lowest = TRUE,
    labels = FALSE
  )

  plot(
    location_grid$x_coord,
    location_grid$y_coord,
    pch = 21,
    bg = spatial_colors[
      color_index
    ],
    asp = 1,
    xlab = "x_coord",
    ylab = "y_coord",
    main = paste(
      "Campo Matérn:",
      epidemic_replicates[j]
    )
  )
}

par(
  old_par
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------
# 24. EXPORTACAO OPCIONAL
# -------------------------------------------------------------

# writexl::write_xlsx(
#   sim_data_spatial_replicate,
#   "sim_data_spatial_replicate.xlsx"
# )
#
# writexl::write_xlsx(
#   simulation_truth_spatial_replicate,
#   "simulation_truth_spatial_replicate.xlsx"
# )

writexl::write_xlsx(
  sim_data_spatial_replicate,
  "sim_data_spatial_replicate.xlsx"
)
```

```{r}
best_model_id <- best$model_id[1]

best_lag <- ens$lag_data |>
  dplyr::filter(model_id == best_model_id) |>
  dplyr::select(
    var,
    lag,
    best_model_contribution = contribution
  )

ensemble_lag <- ens$ensemble_by_lag |>
  dplyr::select(
    var,
    lag,
    ensemble_contribution,
    ensemble_percent_contribution
  )

lag_compare <- dplyr::left_join(
  best_lag,
  ensemble_lag,
  by = c("var", "lag")
)

lag_compare
```

```{r}
lag_compare <- lag_compare |>
  dplyr::group_by(var) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    best_model_percent_contribution =
      100 * abs(best_model_contribution) /
      sum(abs(best_model_contribution), na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

plot_df <- lag_compare |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(best_model_contribution, ensemble_contribution),
    names_to = "source",
    values_to = "contribution"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    source = dplyr::recode(
      source,
      best_model_contribution = "Best model",
      ensemble_contribution = "Lag ensemble"
    )
  )

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = lag, y = contribution, color = source)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ var, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Lag",
    y = "Lag-specific contribution",
    color = NULL,
    title = "Lag-specific contribution: best model vs lag ensemble"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
plot_pct <- lag_compare |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(best_model_percent_contribution, ensemble_percent_contribution),
    names_to = "source",
    values_to = "percent_contribution"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    source = dplyr::recode(
      source,
      best_model_percent_contribution = "Best model",
      ensemble_percent_contribution = "Lag ensemble"
    )
  )

ggplot(plot_pct, aes(x = lag, y = percent_contribution, color = source)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ var, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Lag",
    y = "Relative contribution (%)",
    color = NULL,
    title = "Relative lag importance: best model vs lag ensemble"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
lag_distance <- lag_compare |>
  dplyr::group_by(var) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    rmse_contribution = sqrt(mean(
      (best_model_contribution - ensemble_contribution)^2,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )),
    correlation = stats::cor(
      best_model_contribution,
      ensemble_contribution,
      use = "complete.obs"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

lag_distance
```

```{r}
lag_compare |>
  dplyr::filter(var == "rain") |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    min_best = min(best_model_contribution, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_best = max(best_model_contribution, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_ensemble = min(ensemble_contribution, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_ensemble = max(ensemble_contribution, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_abs_best = mean(abs(best_model_contribution), na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_abs_ensemble = mean(abs(ensemble_contribution), na.rm = TRUE),
    rmse_relative_to_best =
      sqrt(mean((best_model_contribution - ensemble_contribution)^2, na.rm = TRUE)) /
      mean(abs(best_model_contribution), na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

# Lag-specific animation

## tmean

```{r}

library(ggplot2)
library(gganimate)
library(dplyr)

epi_plot <- epi_l |>
  filter(var == "tmean")

tmean_ani = ggplot(
  epi_plot,
  aes(value, effect)
) +
  geom_line(
    color = "#C44E52",
    linewidth = 1.4
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Mean temperature (°C)",
    y = "Effect (%)",
    title = "Lag: {closest_state}"
  ) +
  transition_states(
    lag,
    transition_length = 1,
    state_length = 1
  ) +
  ease_aes("linear")
```

## rain

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(gganimate)
library(dplyr)

rain_ani = ggplot(
```

## wetness

```{r}

library(ggplot2)
library(gganimate)
library(dplyr)

epi_plot <- epi_l |>
  filter(var == "wetness")

wetness_ani = ggplot(
  epi_plot,
  aes(value, effect)
) +
  geom_line(
    color = "#55A868",
    linewidth = 1.4
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    x = "Leaf wetness (hours)",
    y = "Effect (%)",
    title = "Lag: {closest_state}"
  ) +
  transition_states(
    lag,
    transition_length = 1,
    state_length = 1
  ) +
  ease_aes("linear")

anim1 <- animate(tmean_ani, nframes = 85, renderer = magick_renderer())
anim2 <- animate(rain_ani, nframes = 85, renderer = magick_renderer())
anim3 <- animate(wetness_ani, nframes = 85, renderer = magick_renderer())

```

```{r}

combined_frames <- image_append(c(anim1[1], anim2[1],anim3[1]))
for (i in 3:length(anim1)) {
  combined <- image_append(c(anim1[i], anim2[i],anim3[i]))
  combined_frames <- c(combined_frames, combined)
}

anim_save("combined.gif", combined_frames)
```
